If the run does not shift by k, the mechanism is not declaration-count-over-the-whole-list and this statement is wrong.

hypothesis.statement: MWCC numbers this class from r31 downward over the WHOLE local list, not over the initialised group alone, and the uninitialised webs compete for the same run: what decides where the four land is how many uninitialised locals are declared BEFORE them and whether the one the body assigns FIRST (`lastIndex = player->lastTrail;`) is among them. Declaring `slot`/`offset`/`index` ahead of the four pushed the four up into r30..r27; moving `lastIndex` from ahead of them to behind them moved the whole run one register further up, to r31..r28, and put `lastIndex` in r27. The transferable rule for the next function with this residual: when the initialised group has the right ORDER but the wrong REGISTERS, do not permute the group again -- move the UNINITIALISED declarations across it and read savedregs.py --uses after each. NOT A CONTRADICTION of the predecessor's P1/P2 denial: that pair LIFTED the whole body into a static inline (frame 128 -> 120, T140/O137) and is a denial about the guard region and the inline boundary; this lane never lifted anything, kept the frame at 128 and count parity at 140/140, and moved only the ORDER of declarations that both records leave in the outer function.
